P.expected_type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ) (u : WM.Domain n → WM.Target m) (q : WM.Target m) (h_H001 : 1 ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ m) (h_H002 : ContDiffOn ℝ WM.smoothOrder u (WM.positive n)) (h_H003 : ‖q‖ = 1) (h_H004 : ∀ x : WM.Space n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ‖u (x,t)‖ = 1) (h_H005 : ∀ x : WM.Space n, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, WM.dtt u (x,t) - WM.lap u (x,t) = a • u (x,t)) (h_H006 : ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (WM.Space n), IsCompact C ∧ ∀ x : WM.Space n, ∀ r : ℝ, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc s t → u (x,r) = q), WM.conservation u

correspondence.explanation: All original parameters and H001–H006 are retained: positive natural dimensions, the smooth positive-time sphere-valued map, the fixed unit vector, pointwise existence of a real normality scalar without regularity, and one compact spatial support set for each closed positive time interval. Fin coordinates enumerate the same real coordinate spaces, with Euclidean value norm and product Lebesgue measure. The total-time u encoding restricts to the original map; every original map extends arbitrarily to nonpositive times, and all positive-time derivatives and hypotheses are unchanged because they are local on an open set. Thus restriction and extension preserve both directions of the conditional theorem, with no extra boundary condition. Under these hypotheses WM.conservation asserts integrability at every positive time, HasDerivAt E 0 at every positive time, and equality of energies for every positive pair. HasDerivAt E 0 is equivalent to differentiability together with E'=0 (HasDerivAt.deriv and the derivative of a differentiable function give the two directions). The energy definition is exactly ∫(‖u_t‖²+Σj‖u_xj‖²), with no factor 1/2. Its integral has the usual finite real value by the first conjunct. This is the whole source target, including constancy, with no time-zero assertion. There are no external E roots in this source; M001–M004 are library theorems rather than project assumptions.
